summary: Lewis and Clark NF lookout on Elk Peak in the Castle Mountains: 1922 station, 1938 foreman, listed as removed; no design or removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source describes what remains on the summit

events.note: Forestry lookout station on Elk Peak named in a planned seven-mile telephone line (Great Falls Tribune item, May 1922).
Joseph W. Nawrocki named as summer foreman lookout (Independent Record, July 1938).

evidence.supports: Elk Peak is the highest point of the Castle Mountains
island range east of White Sulphur Springs in Meagher County
evidence.quote: island range east of White Sulphur Springs in Meagher County

evidence.supports: officially called Castle Peak for a time
evidence.quote: Elk Peak was officially known as Castle Peak for a time.

evidence.supports: May 1922 Great Falls Tribune item: seven-mile telephone line to the forestry lookout station on Elk Peak
evidence.quote: seven miles of line will be constructed from Four Mile ranger station to the forestry lookout station on Elk Peak, the summit of the Castle Mountains.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one Forest Lookouts page quoting 1922 and 1938 newspaper items, plus Wikipedia for the range. No build date, design, height or removal date found in the sources read. Elevation differs: Montana History Portal 8566 ft, Wikipedia 8,589 ft (not used in the story). Elk Peak does not appear in the FFLA Meagher County rows checked.
